the model says the meaning changed: A failing or regressed test is now dropped from failing/regression and treated as merely unverified when its failing run's commit is outside this checkout's history and the covered code differs, which weakens "a failure stays until a run passes it" and the regression and drift reporting in EX-1, EX-2, EX-3 and EX-7 (a rebase or amend triggers it, as the code's own shortcut note admits).; brought to the owner as a card: You asked that a merge is never green while an affected acceptance test lacks a passing run, and that regressions and failing tests hold the merge until fixed. The requirement says the same: a failure stays until a run passes it.

The change adds an exception. A failure is no longer counted if every run that failed the test was on a commit outside this checkout's history and the code the test covers is now different. The aim seems to be to stop one worktree's failures from showing up as failures in another.

An affected test in this situation still holds the merge, but as "unverified" rather than as a failure or regression. However, it also disappears from the list of unresolved regressions, so a regression can stop being reported without any run passing it. This also happens after a rebase or amend, as the code's own note admits. A real failure in this checkout could then lose its failing or regression label and drop out of what drift and status report, with no run having passed it (EX-1, EX-2, EX-3 and EX-7 describe the behaviour at risk).

What is unclear is whether you wanted this. The change looks deliberate, but no owner prompt was recorded for the turn that probably made it, and neither the requirement nor your intent mentions failures from other worktrees.; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Keep the change, but first make it record which worktree ran the test, so a rebase or amend can't clear a real failure") does and leaves undone; what option 2 ("Keep the change as it is, accept the rebase and amend gap, and reword the requirement to exempt failures from other worktrees") does and leaves undone; what option 3 ("Undo the change: any recorded failure stays until a run passes it, even if it came from another worktree") does and leaves undone; why the recommended option is recommended (iaso stale card SR-254#7 --consequences "..." --why "...")
